# West Virginia, United States Genealogy

[West Virginia](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/West_Virginia,_United_States_Genealogy "West Virginia, United States Genealogy") was admitted to the union as the 35th state on 20 June 1863, having separated from [Virginia](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Virginia,_United_States_Genealogy "Virginia, United States Genealogy") during the Civil War. It was created from the state of Virginia.

## Background

West Virginia's creation as a separate state resulted from the political and military divisions of the Civil War. The northwestern counties of Virginia, which had fewer enslaved persons and stronger Unionist sentiment, voted to form a separate state. The process began in 1861 and concluded when West Virginia was admitted on June 20, 1863.

For genealogical research, this boundary change is significant: an ancestor described as "born in Virginia" before 1863 may have been born in the area that became West Virginia. Many genealogy records are kept on the county level in the United States.

## County Formation

West Virginia was formed from 50 counties of Virginia.

## Key Repositories

- **West Virginia State Archives** — holds state-level records post-1863
